justification: A dormitory is a room students share, and a dirty one is the standing joke about student life.
An astronomer is, quite literally, someone who stares at the moon.
A schoolmaster works in the classroom, so the letters spell the job’s own setting.
Eyes are what see, so the anagram says what the input does.
A debit card is the card people rely on when they have no credit, or bad credit.

Boeing builds some of the largest airliners in the world, including the 747, long called the jumbo jet.

Testing a device for evidence is part of a modern detective’s work.

An admirer who wins over the one they admire may end up married, which turns one word into the other.

Breaking Bad follows a chemistry teacher who cooks meth for a drug ring, which “bad bake ring” describes.
British Airways flies Brits by air, and the anagram keeps both air and Brits.
Britney Spears lived through years of intense press attention to her private life, and the anagram joins press and brain.

For years photographers followed Britney Spears everywhere, and “bye press train” reads like waving them off.
Broadway is home to the Tony Awards, which is what “award” nods to.

An evangelist acts as a living agent of a faith, spreading its message in person.
Frances Tiafoe is a tennis player, and a fair foe and a set both belong to the sport.
Rue means sorrow, which is what a funeral holds.
Another reading of Goldman Sachs that spells a scam, a jab at a bank that has paid large settlements over its conduct.
Great Britain is famous for its rain, and “big treat rain” makes a joke of it.
Another reading of Great Britain that finds great rain in the name of a famously wet country.
Harley-Davidson motorcycles are built for long days on the open road, which “overland” suggests.
Harry Potter is the hero of the books, and the anagram keeps the word hero.
To parry is to block a blow, which Harry does in the wizard duels of the books.
The song Hotel California is about a place its guests can never really leave, and “fail her location” hints at being lost there.
The iPhone has long been sold as the fashionable phone, the hip one.
Los Angeles is a city of renters and long studio deals, and “long leases” nods to both.
Margaret Thatcher was nicknamed the Iron Lady, so calling her “that great charmer” is an ironic twist.
New York City is a city of work and money, and the anagram lists city, yen and work.
Said aloud, Nottingham starts much like “nothing”, which the anagram brings out.
A PlayStation is what people sit down to play, which “sat into play” describes.
The clear skies over the Sahara Desert are known for bright stars overhead.

Slot machines are built on repeated small losses and a compulsive pull, which “the manic loss” describes.
Softheartedness means being easily moved to sadness, and the anagram keeps that word.
Ditches line the fields and lanes of the countryside.
The anagram keeps the word detect, which is what detectives do.
Earthquakes and Quakers share the word quake, a pun the anagram leans on.
Earthquakes make the ground quake, and “hearts quake” turns that into fear.
An earthquake is both a quake and a threat, and the anagram names the two.
The Lord of the Rings is full of elves, and the anagram finds one.
The Lord of the Rings sets hordes of orcs against the free peoples, which “hordes” recalls.
The Sound of Music has the song “Do-Re-Mi”, whose opening line is about a doe, and the anagram keeps that word.
The title’s own question comes back rearranged, with married, tied and why all still in it.
